stem.text: The temperature of a liquid in a laboratory flask is modeled by \( H(t) = 115 - 55 e^{- \frac{t}{10}} \) degrees Celsius, for \( 0 \le t \le 30 \), where t is measured in minutes. Using a calculator, find \( H'(8) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( H'(8) = 2.471 \), so at time t = 8 minutes the temperature of the liquid is increasing at a rate of 2.471 degrees Celsius per minute.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the model to get the rate, \( H'(t) = \frac{11 e^{- \frac{t}{10}}}{2} \).
With a calculator, \( H'(8) = 2.471 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so at time t = 8 minutes the temperature of the liquid is increasing at a rate of 2.471 degrees Celsius per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change
